characters: A child on a safe play area watching a ball roll toward a road, then calling an adult who fetches it.

narrationPlan.voice: A bouncy voice that stops firmly on “Stop!”
narrationPlan.pace: Quick, then a firm stop (about 70 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A bouncing beat that stops at the word Stop, then a calm tune (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Road safety matters for children in towns and villages across Ghana. The rhyme is original.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check that the rule (do not chase a ball into a road; ask an adult) is clear and that nothing here frightens children.

pages.brief: Warm hand-painted gouache scene, landscape 4:3, following the character notes exactly. A red ball rolling out of a play area. Keep a calm, uncluttered area for text.
pages.narration: Bounce and then roll your hands.

pages.brief: Warm hand-painted gouache scene, landscape 4:3, following the character notes exactly. A child holding up a hand, standing still. Keep a calm, uncluttered area for text.
pages.narration: Hold up your hand like a stop sign.

pages.brief: Warm hand-painted gouache scene, landscape 4:3, following the character notes exactly. A child calling an adult. Keep a calm, uncluttered area for text.
pages.narration: Cup your hands around your mouth.

pages.brief: Warm hand-painted gouache scene, landscape 4:3, following the character notes exactly. An adult handing the ball back to a child. Keep a calm, uncluttered area for text.
pages.narration: Say thank you with a smile.

teacherGuide.overview: A short safety rhyme. Form: four couplets. Rhyming pairs: red/ahead, run/fun, see/me, you/through. It teaches road safety and asking for help.
learningGoals: Say what to do if a ball rolls toward a road.
beforeReading: Ask: where is a safe place to play ball?
whileReading: Stop sharply on the word Stop and let children freeze.
afterReading: Play a freeze game: bounce, then stop on a signal.
discussion: Whom can you ask for help?
reflection: Where is your safe play place?

support: Act the story with a soft ball and a taped line.
stretch: Draw a safe play area with a fence.

culturalNotes: Road safety matters for children in towns and villages across Ghana. The rhyme is original.
localiseThis: Name the real safe play places near the school. Make sure each child knows who the nearest adult is.
